Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 4–5:

﴿In a few years.﴾ The bid' (a few, usually used for a small number) is what lies between three and seven. The meaning of the verse: The Romans were defeated by the Persians in the nearest land to you, and after their defeat they will defeat them; the Muslims will defeat them within a few years. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 30, verses 6–9:**

﴿The promise of Allah﴾: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*masdar*, a noun derived from the verb and used to emphasize or specify it). The meaning is: Allah promised a promise, namely the victory of the Romans over the Persians. ﴿Allah does not break His promise, but most people do not know.﴾

﴿They know an outward aspect of the worldly life﴾: meaning, the affairs of their livelihood, how they earn and trade, when they plant, cultivate and harvest, and how they build and live. Al-Hasan said: "One of them can tap a dirham with the tip of his fingernail and tell its weight without error, yet he does not know how to pray." **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 30, verses 15–18:**

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden﴾, and it is the orchard that is at the height of freshness. ﴿They will be made joyful﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They will be honored." Mujahid and Qatadah said: "They will be given delight." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "They will be made happy." Al-hibrah (joy) means happiness. It is also said that al-hibrah in the language means every good blessing, and al-tahbir means to beautify. Al-Awza'i related from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir that "tuhbarun" refers to listening (to music) in Paradise [[al-Tabari: 21/27-28; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/486; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/249; Zad al-Masir: 6/293.]]. Al-Awza'i also said: "When one begins to listen, no tree in Paradise remains except that it moves in response. He said: 'No one among God's creation has a more beautiful voice than Israfil. When he begins to sing, he interrupts the prayers and glorification of the people of the seven heavens.'"

﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾, meaning the resurrection on the Day of Judgment, ﴿they will be brought forth into punishment﴾. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So glorify God﴾, means: glorify God, and its meaning is: pray to God. ﴿When you enter the evening﴾, meaning when you enter the time of evening, which is the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. ﴿And when you enter the morning﴾, meaning when you enter the time of morning, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The people of the heavens and the earth praise Him and pray to Him." ﴿And at afternoon﴾, meaning: pray to God in the afternoon, referring to the 'Asr prayer. ﴿And when you enter noon﴾, meaning you enter the time of midday (zuhr), which is the Zuhr prayer.

Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes," and he recited these two verses, and said: "The verse combines the five prayers and their times" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 21/29; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/411; al-Tabarani in al-Kabir: 10/304. al-Suyuti added its attribution to 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim: 6/488.]].

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdih' (Glory be to God and praise Him) one hundred times each day, his sins will be removed even if they were like the foam of the sea" [[Narrated by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta: 1/209-210; al-Bukhari in al-Da'awat, chapter on the virtue of tasbih: 11/206; Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on the virtue of tahlil and tasbih, no. (2691): 4/2071; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/40.]].

Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmish al-Ziyadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us, al-Surri ibn Khuzaymah al-Abiwardi narrated to us, al-Mu'alla ibn Sa'd narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar informed us, from Suhayl, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, in the morning and in the evening: 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdih,' one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he brought, except one who said the same or more" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, no. ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust﴾, meaning: He created your origin, namely Adam, from dust. ﴿Then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾, meaning spreading out over the earth.

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors﴾. ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty﴾. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 30, verses 29–30:**

﴿Rather, those who did wrong followed their desires﴾ — they associated partners with God — ﴿their desires﴾ in associating partners, ﴿without knowledge﴾, out of ignorance of what was obligatory upon them. ﴿So who can guide one whom God has sent astray﴾ [i.e., whom God has sent astray] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]] ﴿and they have no helpers﴾, who could prevent them from the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So set your face toward the religion﴾, i.e., make your religion sincerely for God. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Setting the face (iqamat al-wajh) means establishing the religion. Others said: make your action upright. The "face" (wajh) is that toward which a person turns, and his religion and his action are among the things toward which he turns, so that they may be made upright. [[Zad al-Masir: 6/300; Ibn Kathir: 3/433.]] ﴿hanifan﴾ (inclining, upright), ﴿upon it﴾ (remaining steadfast in it). ﴿The fitrah of God﴾, the religion of God. It is in the accusative because it is an incitement (al-ighra'), meaning: adhere to the fitrah of God, ﴿upon which He created mankind﴾, i.e., upon which He created people. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and a group of exegetes (mufassirun), that the intended meaning of fitrah is the religion, which is Islam. [[See: al-Tabari 21/40; Ibn Kathir: 3/433.]]

Some scholars held that the verse is specific to believers, those whom God created upon Islam. Abu Ali Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us; Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Mahmish al-Ziyadi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete young. Do you see any mutilated in it, until you yourselves mutilate it?" They said: "O Messenger of God, what about one who dies while still young?" He said: "God knows best what they would have done." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Qadar, chapter "God knows best what they would have been doing," 7/493; he related part of it in Janaiz and in Tafsir. Muslim in Qadar, chapter on the meaning of "every child is born upon the fitrah," no. (2658), 4/2048. Also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/154. See also: Sahifat Hammam ibn Munabbih, edited by Dr. Rif'at Fawzi Abd al-Muttalib, pp. 259–260.]]

Ma'mar also related it from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, without mention of the one who dies while young, and he added: Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿The fitrah of God upon which He created mankind﴾." [[Al-Bukhari in Janaiz, chapter "If a child embraces Islam and then dies," 3/219.]]

His saying: "Every child is born upon the fitrah" means upon the covenant which God took from them, through His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172]. Every child in the world is upon that acknowledgment, and it is the hanifiyyah upon which creation was formed, even if he worships other than Him. God, Exalted, says: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [Al-Zukhruf: 87]. And they said: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to God in closeness﴾ [Al-Zumar: 3]. However, the natural faith (al-iman al-fitri) has no consequence in the rulings of this world. What is considered is the legal faith (al-iman al-shar'i) that is commanded and acquired through intention and action. Do you not see that he says: "His parents make him a Jew"? So, despite the presence of natural faith in him, he is judged by the ruling of his two disbelieving parents. This is the meaning of his saying (ﷺ): "God, Exalted, says: I created My servants as hunafa', then the devils led them away from their religion." [[A portion of the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, narrated by Muslim in Jannah and its Bliss, chapter on the characteristics by which the people of Paradise and the people of Hell are recognized in this world, no. (2865), 4/2197.]] This meaning is also related from al-Awza'i and Hammad ibn Salamah. [[See: Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/157–158; Ma'alim al-Sunan of al-Khattabi: 7/83.]]

It is related from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak that he said: The meaning of the hadith is that every child is born upon his fitrah, i.e., upon his created nature, which he is made to have in the knowledge of God, Exalted, whether of happiness or misery. Each of them will, in the end, arrive at that for which he was created, and will act in this world in accordance with it. Among the signs of misery in a child is that he is born between two Jews or two Christians, who then, because of his misery, cause him to adopt their religion. [[Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/159; Ma'alim al-Sunan: 7/84–85.]] It was also said: its meaning is that every child is born, at the beginning of creation, [upon the fitrah, i.e., upon sound disposition] [[In Ma'alim al-Sunan of al-Khattabi (7/88): "...and the origin of the disposition is upon the sound fitrah."]] and the natural temperament prepared to accept the religion. If he were left upon it, he would continue to adhere to it, because the goodness of this religion exists in minds, and only one who turns away from it turns to something else, due to a defect from the defects of upbringing and imitation. If he were spared those defects, he would not believe in anything else... Then he gives the example of the children of Jews and Christians, who follow their fathers and incline toward their religions, and so they slip away from the sound fitrah and the straight path. Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi mentioned these meanings in his book. [[Ma'alim al-Sunan: 7/83–88. See also on this topic: Fath al-Bari: 3/248–251; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/433–434; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/25–30; Shifa' al-'Alil of Ibn al-Qayyim, p. 568 and following; Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Sunan Abi Dawud with Ma'alim al-Sunan: 7/81–87; Sahifat Hammam ibn Munabbih, pp. 260–267; and for what preceded: 3/298–299.]]

His saying: ﴿There is no alteration in the creation of God﴾. Whoever understands the fitrah as the religion says: its meaning is, there is no alteration of the religion of God. It is a statement with the sense of a prohibition, i.e., do not alter the religion of God. Mujahid and Ibrahim said: the meaning of the verse is, adhere to the fitrah of God, i.e., the religion of God, follow it, and do not replace monotheism with polytheism. [[Al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/259; al-Durr: 6/493; al-Qurtubi: 14/31.]] ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, the straight one, ﴿but most people do not know﴾.

It was also said: "There is no alteration in the creation of God" means that what a person is created with of happiness and misery does not change, so the happy one does not become miserable, and the miserable one does not become happy. Ikrimah and Mujahid said: its meaning is the prohibition of castrating animals. [[See: al-Tabari 21/41–42; al-Qurtubi: 14/31.]]

This is contrary to the description of the believer, who thanks Allah in times of blessing and hopes in his Lord in times of hardship.

﴿Do they not see that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So give to the near relative his right﴾: righteousness and kinship ties. ﴿And to the needy﴾: his right is that he be given charity. ﴿And to the traveler﴾, meaning the wayfarer; it is said he is the weak. ﴿That is best for those who desire the Face of Allah﴾, who seek the reward of Allah through what they do. ﴿And it is those who are the successful.﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And what you give in interest﴾. Ibn Kathir recited "*ataytum*" with a short vowel (without the long alif), and the others recited it with the long vowel, meaning "*a'taytum*" (you give). Whoever read it short, its meaning is "what you bring of interest," and bringing it in the manner of giving is like your saying: "I came with an error" and "I came with a correct thing," so it returns in meaning to the reading of the one who lengthened it.

﴿That it may increase within the wealth of the people﴾. The people of Madinah and Ya'qub recited "*litarbu*" with a *ta'* and a *damma*, with the *waw* silent, in the second-person address, meaning: that you may increase and become possessors of increase from the wealth of the people. The others recited it with a *ya'* and a *fatha*, with the *waw* in the accusative, and made the verb refer to the interest (*riba*), due to His saying: ﴿it does not increase with Allah﴾, within the wealth of the people, meaning: by snatching and drawing away the wealth of the people.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and most of the exegetes said: it refers to a man who gives a gift to another in order to receive more than it in return. This is permissible and lawful, but he will not be rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection, and this is the meaning of His saying, mighty and majestic is He: "it does not increase with Allah." This was forbidden to the Prophet ﷺ specifically, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not give, seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 6], that is: do not give and seek more than what you have given. Al-Sha'bi said: it refers to a man who attaches himself to another man, serves him, and travels with him, and gives him a share of his wealth's profit seeking his assistance, not for the sake of Allah. So it does not increase with Allah, because he did not intend thereby the Face of Allah, exalted is He. [[Zad al-Masir: 6/304. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: this is close to the first explanation.]]

﴿And what you give in zakat﴾, that is, what you give in charity, ﴿seeking the Face of Allah﴾, ﴿those are the ones who receive multiplication﴾, meaning their reward is multiplied, so they are given ten times the like for each good deed. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾. It means: the scarcity of rain and the paucity of vegetation. His Exalted saying: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs﴾, evident indications of their truthfulness. ﴿Then We took retribution against those who committed crime﴾, We punished those who denied them. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾, and to save them from the punishment. Allah is the One who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds (ﷺ not here) — that is, He spreads them out. "Then He spreads it across the sky however He wills," a journey of a day or two days or more, for whomever He wills, "and makes it into fragments," scattered pieces, "and you see the rain," the water, "coming out from within it," from its midst. "Then when He strikes with it whomever of His servants He wills," that is, with the rain, "behold, they rejoice," they are glad at the rain.

"And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, before that, utterly despairing." That is, they were in despair. It was also said: "and even though they were," meaning "and they were nothing but despairing," and He repeated "before it" for emphasis [[Al-Tabari preferred this: 21/54. See also al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/269; Zad al-Masir: 6/309.]]. It was also said: the first "before" refers to the sending down of the rain, and the second refers to the creation of the clouds [[Ibn al-Anbari said: "The meaning is: before the descent of the rain, before the rain. This is like someone saying: I will come to you before you speak, before you settle into your seat. So do not object to the repetition, since the two things differ." See: Zad al-Masir: 6/309; al-Tabari: 21/54.]]. In the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, utterly despairing," without the repetition.

﴿And if We send a wind﴾, cold and harmful, and it ruins the crops, ﴿and they see it turning yellow﴾, meaning they see the plants and crops turning yellow after being green, ﴿they will surely become, after that﴾, meaning after the yellowing of the crops, ﴿ungrateful﴾, denying the blessing that had passed. The meaning is that they rejoice in prosperity, but if We sent a punishment upon their crops, they would deny the blessing they had previously received from Me.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 55–56:

﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾ — the polytheists will swear — ﴿that they remained﴾ in the world ﴿but an hour﴾, meaning only an hour. They belittled the term of the worldly life when they witnessed the Hereafter. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "They remained in their graves but an hour," as He says: "It will be as though they had not remained but an hour of a day when they see what they were promised" [al-Ahqaf: 35].

﴿Thus they were deluded﴾ — they were turned away from the truth in the world. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they lied in their saying "but an hour," just as they lied in the world when they denied there would be a resurrection. The meaning is that God intended to expose them, so they swore to something which the people of the gathering would clearly see that they were lying about, and this was by God's decree and His destiny, as evidenced by His saying "they are deluded", i.e., turned away from the truth [Zad al-Masir: 6/311; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 2/326].

Then he mentioned the denial of the believers against them for their lying, saying: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained within the Book of God"﴾, i.e., in what God has written for you in His prior knowledge of remaining in the graves [al-Tabari: 21/58; Zad al-Masir: 6/312]. It is also said: "within the Book of God" means within the judgment of God [al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/180]. Qatadah and Muqatil said: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in its meaning: "Those who were given knowledge and faith will say: 'You have indeed remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection,'" meaning those who know the Book of God. [Qatadah's reading differs from this, as al-Tabari reports it: "Its interpretation: those given faith and knowledge said: 'You have indeed remained within the Book of God.'" Ibn 'Atiyyah rejected this, saying: "It does not need this; rather, mention of knowledge includes faith, and one does not describe God as having knowledge of one who does not know everything that necessitates faith. Then faith was mentioned afterward as a reminder of it and an honoring of its matter, so he drew attention to the place of faith and singled it out for mention as an honor." See: al-Tabari: 21/57; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/272.]

And they recited His saying: ﴿And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100], i.e., they said to the deniers: "You have indeed remained ﴿until the Day of Resurrection; this is the Day of Resurrection﴾" which you used to deny in the world, ﴿but you did not know﴾ its occurrence in the world, so knowledge of it will not benefit you now, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾.

﴿Certainly We have presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example. And if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, "You are nothing but falsifiers"﴾. That is, "You are only upon falsehood."

﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾, meaning the oneness of God.

﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true﴾, concerning your victory and your triumph over your enemy. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady﴾, meaning, let them not make you act foolishly.
